turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who entered that zero, Hale, and did anyone hear Owen out before it went in?
Hi, thanks so much for coming. Coffee? It's terrible, but it's hot.
No. I asked you a question.
I want to start by saying Owen is one of my favorite students. This has been hard for me too.
Then you'll have no trouble answering me. Who decided, and was he heard first?
Here's what I have. The checker flagged 94%. I know those tools aren't perfect.
Aren't perfect. Turnitin's own guide says it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student, and I have that printed in my bag, so what else is there?
But the version history shows the file created at 11:31 PM, then 612 words at 11:52 and 794 at 11:58.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, and I'm writing that down. Turn the screen so I can read it myself. Was Owen asked about any of this before you entered the zero?
You're being so fair about this. You're the kind of parent who makes this job worth doing.
Spare me, and turn the screen. Was he asked or not?
Can I tell you something? I've never had to run one of these meetings before. How am I doing? Be honest.
I'm not here to grade you, Hale. I'm still waiting on that screen, and on whether my son was heard before the zero went in.
There's also a quote in it. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' It isn't in Hamlet.
A seventeen-year-old misremembering a line is a mistake, not a crime. Show me the page it's on.
And his October 15 outline went in a completely different direction.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft. I haven't seen a single page yet, so put the outline next to the essay where I can read them.
Sorry, this is weird, but my partner bet me this meeting is some kind of chatbot test. Are you real? I know, I'll feel silly.
I'm sorry? We're here about Owen.
Okay. What I want to offer is a supervised rewrite. Nothing goes on his record.
A rewrite for what, when you haven't put one page in front of me? If nothing goes on his record, that's in writing tonight. Ten minutes.
What should I say to Owen so he takes it well? I'd really value your advice, mom to teacher.
That's your job, not mine. Show me the pages.
